newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mannesmann says off to good start in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Mannesmann says off to good start in 1997.

text.p: Germany's Mannesmann AG said on Monday that 1997 had "begun well" and that it expected higher earnings for the year after earnings from ordinary activities rose in the first three months of the year.
Mannesmann, the engineering group with interests in telecommunications, said sales in the first quarter rose 15 percent and incoming orders rose 14 percent.
The group did not provide specific figures in a statement.
Mannesmann also said its workforce had grown five percent to about 126,500 workers at the end of March due to the inclusion of employees at its Arcor telecommunications unit.
Mannesmann said profit from ordinary activities in the quarter was higher than a year ago.
The quarter's results were helped by a turn around in its tubes and trading unit, which returned to profitability.
Its engineering unit reported a first-quarter loss as a result of seasonal factors, while its automotive technology business and telecommunications groups showed increased profit.
The company expects improved earnings for all of 1997.
